preamble: The retroflex fricative [ʂ] is often pronounced as the alveolar fricative [s] in Southern Mandarin and Taiwanese Mandarin phonology. In Polish dialects with mazurzenie (Masovia, Masuria, most of Lesser Poland, parts of Silesia), standard sz [ʂ] corresponds to s [s], so sześć 'six' is [sɛɕt͡ɕ] and szyty 'sewn' becomes homophonous with syty 'full'. Its origin is debated: Koneczna derives it directly from the 16th-century depalatalization of the older palato-alveolars /ʃ, ʒ, t͡ʃ, d͡ʒ/, which gave retroflexes elsewhere but dentals here, while Kuryłowicz argues that archaic dialects adopted the new retroflexes and replaced them with dentals. It is treated here as a synchronic dialect correspondence of standard Polish retroflex cz, sz, ż, dż [t͡ʂ ʂ ʐ d͡ʐ] to mazurating c, s, z, dz. In Southern Quechua (Quechua II-C), Proto-Quechuan *ʂ became s (*iʂkaj > iskaj 'two').
